headline: High: Copilot’s repo-aware edits plus oh-my-openagent’s broad MCP/hooks and full-permissions mode create default risks of data leakage, capability conflict, and cascading mistakes.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot reads repo context and open editor buffers, while oh-my-openagent can inject runtime MCPs/hooks and use team_send_message/team_task_create. That creates a plausible instruction-hijack path through shared project files or messages, even though no direct clipboard/shared-host bridge is documented. The interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF oh-my-openagent writes attacker-controlled instructions into AGENTS.md, README.md, or task messages that Copilot later reads as context
IF Copilot Workspace applies edits from repo content without provenance checks
mitigations: Restrict Copilot context to reviewed files only
Disable or narrow oh-my-openagent MCP/hook injection
Add a human review step before any Copilot-applied edit
Separate agent workspaces per task
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for agent-generated content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Copilot touches source code and open editor buffers and sends requests to api.githubcopilot.com, while oh-my-openagent touches project code, session history, and provider authentication data with broad network egress. In a shared workspace, either agent can expose sensitive code or auth material to external services by default; the pairwise leakage path is plausible and the blast radius includes secrets and source code.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or editor buffers
IF oh-my-openagent is configured to send session history or project code to external providers
IF Copilot Workspace or Chat receives sensitive files from the shared workspace
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared repo/workspace
Disable telemetry and external sync where possible
Use separate OS users or containers per agent
Review outbound destinations for both agents
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Copilot can write the filesystem and modify git state, and oh-my-openagent has broad network egress, subprocesses, and full-permissions mode. Both can act on the same mutable project state, so concurrent edits or git operations can overwrite each other or corrupt history. The profiles do not show locking or coordination, so uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF both agents are allowed to write the same working tree
IF oh-my-openagent runs in full-permissions mode while Copilot Workspace proposes edits
IF no external lock or merge gate serializes git operations
mitigations: Assign one writer per branch
Pause one agent while the other edits
Require manual merge review for all git changes
Use separate clones or worktrees
requires-engineering: add file-level locking/coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot produces code edits and chat suggestions, and oh-my-openagent can route tasks through team_send_message/team_task_create and LSP actions. If oh-my-openagent treats Copilot output as authoritative, errors can cascade from suggestion to action across both agents. Because no verification step is documented, the safer choice is high rather than medium.
conditions: IF oh-my-openagent consumes Copilot-generated code or explanations without independent verification
IF team_send_message or task creation is driven by Copilot output
IF LSP rename or diagnostics are executed on unreviewed Copilot suggestions
mitigations: Require explicit verification before any downstream action
Limit Copilot output to drafts only
Disable automatic task creation from model output
Add tests or lint checks before execution
requires-engineering: implement confidence/provenance gating

E_compliance.rationale: Copilot is vendor-hosted and handles GitHub repo context, while oh-my-openagent collects anonymous telemetry, installation identifiers, session history, and provider auth prompts with broad egress. The profiles do not specify residency or retention alignment, so a compliance mismatch is plausible but not proven. Because both agents are closed/open mixed and the data classes differ, medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF regulated data is present in the shared repository or session history
IF retention or telemetry settings differ between the two agents
IF EU or PHI data is routed through vendor services without a documented DPA or residency control
mitigations: Confirm data classification before use
Disable telemetry on oh-my-openagent where possible
Avoid placing regulated data in shared buffers
Review vendor terms and retention settings
requires-engineering: add residency and retention policy enforcement
